title: Do I always need to replace my roof before going solar?

title: How old is too old for a roof before solar installation?
description: Roofs older than 15 to 20 years often lack sufficient remaining lifespan to support solar panels for their full service life.

title: Can solar panels damage my roof?
description: When installed correctly on a sound roof, solar panels do not damage roofing materials. Problems typically arise when panels are installed on deteriorating roofs.

description: Roof inspections are recommended annually, while solar systems should be reviewed at least once per year or whenever performance changes are noticed.

title: Is solar panel cleaning always necessary?
description: In areas with frequent rain, natural cleaning may help, but dust and debris still accumulate over time. Periodic solar panel cleaning ensures optimal performance.

title: Can roof damage affect solar panel efficiency?
description: Yes. Roof movement, leaks, or structural issues can affect panel alignment and mounting stability, reducing efficiency and increasing risk.

title: Will poor maintenance void warranties?
description: Many manufacturers require proper maintenance documentation. Failure to follow guidelines may void roofing or solar warranties.

title: Should homeowners perform maintenance themselves?
description: Basic visual checks are helpful, but professional inspections are recommended for roof work, electrical components, and solar mounting systems to ensure safety and compliance.

title: Should I inspect my roof after every storm?
description: After major storms, a visual inspection is recommended. Look for missing shingles, debris impact, or signs of water intrusion.

title: How can I reduce the risk of emergency roof leaks?
description: Seasonal inspections, gutter cleaning, and addressing minor damage early are the most effective ways to reduce emergency leak risk.

title: Are snow loads dangerous for residential roofs?
description: Most roofs are designed to handle expected snow loads, but uneven accumulation or drainage issues can increase stress and lead to damage.

title: How do ice dams form on roofs?
description: Ice dams form when warm air melts snow on the roof, and the water refreezes near the eaves. Poor insulation and ventilation are common contributing factors.

title: What should be included in a winter roofing preparation guide?
description: A winter roofing preparation guide should cover inspections of shingles, flashing, gutters, insulation, and ventilation, as well as steps to reduce ice dam risk.

title: What is the best solar battery storage for home use?
description: The best option depends on energy usage, backup needs, and system compatibility. Tesla Powerwall 3 and Enphase IQ10 are both widely used options.

description: Yes, especially when paired with solar panels, though duration depends on usage and available sunlight.

description: Maintenance needs are generally low and limited to inspections and software updates.

title: Are solar batteries covered by warranties?
description: Most systems include performance warranties covering capacity retention over time.

title: Can batteries be added to existing solar systems?
description: In many cases yes, though compatibility should be evaluated.

title: What happens at the end of a solar PPA?
description: Options vary by provider and may include renewing the agreement, purchasing the system, or having it removed.

title: Can I sell my home if I have a solar PPA?
description: Yes, but the agreement usually needs to be transferred to the new owner. This process should be clearly outlined in the contract.

title: Do I qualify for tax credits with a solar PPA?
description: No. Tax credits and incentives typically go to the system owner, which is the solar provider in a PPA arrangement.

title: Is a solar PPA better than buying solar panels?
description: It depends on your financial goals. PPAs reduce upfront costs, while ownership often provides greater long-term savings and control.

title: What is a solar PPA in simple terms?
description: A solar PPA is an agreement where you buy electricity from a solar system installed on your property, but you do not own the system itself.
